correctness.rationale: For uniform f:[n]→[n] conditioned on nonnegative indegrees d with sum n (n≥2), exposing the uniform target multiset gives E[(F)_r]=r!e_r(d)/(n)_r and P_d(z)=Σ_r e_r(d)(z-1)^r/(n)_r. A transfer (A,B)→(A-1,B+1), A≥B+2, increases the elementary symmetric product by δ t² times the unaffected product, δ=A-B-1. The unaffected positive multiplicities have total at most n-2; sampling distinct placement targets by injection defines genuine PGF Q_c(z), making the exact difference δ(z-1)^2 Q_c(z)/[n(n-1)]. Coefficient duality yields the discrete second-difference identity and strict order under every strictly convex phi; the integer majorization chain gives the global comparison. Means remain one, variance (n²-Σ d_i²)/[n(n-1)], extreme one-image and bijection profiles. Independently verified 96 exact balancing identities (not a proof for all n).

originality.rationale: Hansen–Jaworski give the same prescribed/exchangeable-degree random mapping ensemble, but primary material inspected treats cyclic vertices, components and size, not all-convex-loss ordering of fixed loops. Stark counts fixed positions in a repeated-symbol multiset permutation with mean Σ d_i²/n, different from E F=1 in this model. Resultary contains a Bernoulli-pair balancing second-difference theorem, but its independent Bernoulli sums are not this without-replacement map. Classical permanental/rook-polynomial assignment convex-order results might be broader and are retained as priority risk.
